Show an intensity as a flickering flame

Source: R/flame.R
flame.Rd

Draws a flame whose height follows an intensity: the higher the intensity, the taller the flame, the faster it flickers and the more sparks it throws. The flame is made of three layers (outer, middle and core) with a warm glow behind it, and can burn on its own, on a candle or on logs. Useful to show the state of a critical number, such as the number of errors in a process. When the chart scrolls into view, the flame ignites and grows to its height while the value (with show_value = TRUE) counts up.

Usage

flame(
  intensity = 50,
  flame_gradient_colors = c("#fffbe6", "#ffc233", "#e8452c"),
  flame_outline = NULL,
  bg_col = "white",
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL,
  max_intensity = 100,
  base = c("none", "candle", "logs"),
  show_value = FALSE,
  value_suffix = "",
  title_text = NULL,
  title_color = NULL,
  title_font_size = 14,
  label_color = NULL,
  label_font_size = NULL,
  font = "Verdana, Geneva, Tahoma, sans-serif",
  flicker = TRUE,
  sparks = TRUE,
  draggable = FALSE,
  animate = TRUE
)

Arguments

intensity

A non-negative number: the intensity of the flame. The height of the flame grows linearly with it up to max_intensity, where the flame reaches the top of the chart. Defaults to 50.

flame_gradient_colors

A length-3 character vector of colours, from the core of the flame outwards. Defaults to c("#fffbe6", "#ffc233", "#e8452c").

flame_outline

Optional. The colour of an outline drawn around the flame. By default the flame has no outline.

bg_col

The background colour. Defaults to "white". The flame glows more on dark backgrounds.

width

Optional. The width of the chart.

height

Optional. The height of the chart.

max_intensity

The intensity at which the flame reaches its full height. Defaults to 100. Higher intensities do not make the flame taller.

base

What the flame burns on: "none" (the default), "candle" or "logs".

show_value

Logical. Write the intensity below the flame. Defaults to FALSE.

value_suffix

A text added after the value, such as " errors". Defaults to "".

title_text

Optional. A caption below the flame.

title_color

Optional. The colour of the caption. Defaults to label_color.

title_font_size

The font size of the caption. Defaults to 14.

label_color

Optional. The colour of the value. Defaults to dark grey on light backgrounds and light grey on dark ones.

label_font_size

Optional. The font size of the value. By default it depends on the size of the chart.

font

The font family. Defaults to "Verdana, Geneva, Tahoma, sans-serif".

flicker

Logical. Animate the flame. Defaults to TRUE.

sparks

Logical. Show sparks rising from the flame. Defaults to TRUE.

draggable

Logical. Let the viewer change the intensity by dragging or with the arrow keys. Defaults to FALSE.

animate

Logical. Ignite the flame when it first comes into view. Defaults to TRUE.

Value

An r2d3 htmlwidget.

Interactions

  • Move the mouse near the flame: it leans away, as if you were blowing on it.

  • Click the flame: it flares up and throws a burst of sparks.

  • With draggable = TRUE, drag up or down on the flame to set the intensity, or focus the chart (click it or press Tab) and use the arrow keys.

Shiny

Inside Shiny, with r2d3::d3Output("id") and r2d3::renderD3(), clicking the flame sets input$id_clicked to a list with intensity, and, with draggable = TRUE, setting the intensity sets input$id_value to the new intensity. When the chart is re-rendered with a new intensity, the flame grows or shrinks from the old height to the new one.

Examples

flame(intensity = 20)


flame(
  intensity = 80,
  flame_gradient_colors = c("#e0f7ff", "#5ac8fa", "#1d4ed8"),
  bg_col = "#111111",
  base = "logs"
)


flame(
  intensity = 35,
  base = "candle",
  show_value = TRUE,
  value_suffix = " errors",
  title_text = "Failed jobs today"
)
